name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,749

clue.text: So many drunk with cricket group

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about unsteadily, so the letters lurch into a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket team's supporters have been drinking heavily, and a great many of them are drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: All thirteen letters of the first two words and 'cricket' are used; the cricket team picture hides that 'group' means a pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic Monkeys are a Sheffield rock band, and a band is a musical group.

clue.text: Applaud account — one saying little about India

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece is wrapped round another

blocks.note: AC is the usual abbreviation for account
someone who clams up says little, hence a clam
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is praising a report told by a taciturn witness about India.
explanation.walkthrough: A clam is a byword for a person who says little, as in 'clam up'; India goes inside it, and the account abbreviation goes in front: AC + CLA(I)M.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim is to praise loudly and publicly, just as an audience applauds a performer.

clue.text: Time to leave street party that's climactic

definitions.note: an adjective defining a noun; 'that's climactic' describes what a crescendo is

indicators.note: whatever leaves goes away, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a crescent is a curved street of houses
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: Someone must leave a street party just as it reaches its high point.
explanation.walkthrough: CRESCENT loses its T, then DO is added: CRESCEN + DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is the peak or climax of rising intensity, the moment music or excitement becomes loudest.

clue.text: Absurd how harangue ends

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that last letter is wanted

blocks.note: the manner of finishing is 'in an' letter, read as a phrase
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A rant is being mocked for how ridiculously it finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ask how the word 'harangue' ends: it ends 'in an E', which run together spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and senseless, lacking any sensible content, which is close to ridiculous.

clue.text: One to monitor seeing work artist announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out to listeners, so we go by the sound rather than the spelling

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
the Venetian painter Titian, whose name is pronounced 'tishan'

explanation.surface: Someone is sent to keep an eye on a painting while an artist's name is called out.
explanation.walkthrough: OP plus Titian, said out loud, runs together as the answer's pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician tests and looks after people's eyesight, checking how well they can see.

clue.text: Double entendre about woman with strict morals?

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece is wrapped round another

blocks.note: a pun plays on two meanings of a word
a woman's name

explanation.surface: A saucy innuendo is made about a straitlaced woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the joke: a straitlaced woman is exactly the sort who would not enjoy a double entendre made about her.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritan, used adjectively, describes someone rigidly moral and disapproving of pleasure, after the strict Protestant sect.

clue.text: Revolutionary princess rises up behind

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a rani is an Indian princess or queen
a horse that rears rises up on its hind legs

explanation.surface: A rebel princess stands up at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a description of the princess's politics; it turns RANI round.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in arrears means late with payments owed, so behind with what you should have paid.

clue.text: Island girl supplies topic for debate

blocks.note: IS is the abbreviation for island
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman from an island suggests a subject to argue about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supplies' looks like the girl handing something over; it simply joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a matter under discussion or in dispute, the point people argue over.

clue.text: Horse kept by Pathan represented fiery mixture

indicators.note: what is kept by someone is held inside their keeping, so one piece sits within another
to represent is to present again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Pashtun tribesman keeps a horse, depicted as a fiery blend.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroin slang turns the horse into H, which joins the letters of the tribesman's name before the lot is rearranged. A Pathan is a Pashtun of Afghanistan or Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a flammable blend of liquid hydrocarbons distilled from petroleum or coal tar, used as fuel.

clue.text: Giant mushrooms no good for muscle

indicators.note: saying no to something means it is not there, so that letter goes missing

blocks.note: giant means big
ceps are edible wild mushrooms, also called porcini
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Huge mushrooms are claimed to be no use for building muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: BIG CEPS drops its G to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is the large muscle at the front of the upper arm, flexed to show strength.

clue.text: French knight's endless sound in fanfare

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
one thing placed within another sits inside it

blocks.note: a sound argument is a valid one
a fanfare is a noisy welcome, a cheer

explanation.surface: A French knight's arrival is marked by a note heard within a trumpet flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' suggests a noise in the fanfare, but it means valid; that word loses its last letter and goes inside CHEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevalier is the French word for a knight or horseman, a rank in orders such as the Legion of Honour.

clue.text: Writer's answer: put question the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means travelling backwards, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
to pose a question is to put it

explanation.surface: An author replies, complaining that the question was asked badly.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus POSE turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek storyteller credited with the famous fables, so an author.

clue.text: In sound, flood rescue vessel reveals bow

indicators.note: judged by sound rather than spelling, so we listen for a word said the same way

blocks.note: Noah's ark saved his family and the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: Seen through the noise of a flood, a rescue boat shows its front end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' looks like the front of the boat, but it means a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a curved line, the same shape as a bow bent for shooting arrows.

clue.text: Test pilot's emergency propeller?

blocks.note: surface reading: a spare propeller for an aircraft in trouble
setter's reading: the device that propels the pilot out of a failing plane

explanation.walkthrough: A propeller normally drives an aircraft forward; here it is whatever propels the pilot himself clear in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the aircraft seat that fires the occupant out of the cockpit when the plane must be abandoned.

clue.text: See 1
Be up to murder Greens' leader? It's wrong!

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
a leader goes at the front, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: to be is to exist, to live
to do someone in is to murder them
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone is plotting to kill the Green Party's leader, and it's condemned as wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be up' reads as 'be planning', but it is LIVE going up; then DO IN and the Green initial follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Evildoing is wicked behaviour, and a wrong as a noun is an unjust or immoral act.

clue.text: American falls: under the influence, I rang AA

indicators.note: someone under the influence of drink is muddled, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American takes a tumble while drunk and phones Alcoholics Anonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like a verb about someone tripping; with 'American' it names the waterfall. AA here suggests Alcoholics Anonymous, though it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara Falls lie on the border of New York State and Ontario, North American waterfalls.

clue.text: Wren for one in the 1A flying

indicators.note: things flying about are scattered, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first word of the answer to 1 across

explanation.surface: A little bird is seen flying in the frozen north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wren' looks like the bird, which suits 'flying'; it is Sir Christopher Wren, designer of St Paul's Cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Wren was the celebrated English designer of buildings, so an example of that profession.

clue.text: Pirate almost snatching gold to add to small coins

indicators.note: almost all of something is short of the whole, so the last letter is lost
whatever snatches something grabs it and holds it within
adding one thing to another joins them end to end

blocks.note: Captain Flint is the pirate in Treasure Island
or is gold in heraldry
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A pirate grabs gold to add to his hoard of small change.
explanation.walkthrough: FLINT loses its T, takes in OR, and S is added: FL(OR)IN + S. A florin was a British two-shilling coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Florins are coins: the name was used for an old British two-shilling piece and for gold coins of Florence.

clue.text: Anger seen after second month with fever

indicators.note: being seen after something means coming behind it in the line, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: FEB is the calendar abbreviation for February
to rile someone is to anger them

explanation.surface: Someone flares up in temper after coming down with a fever in February.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen after' puts the anger word behind the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Febrile is the medical adjective for feverish, suffering from a raised temperature.

clue.text: Scuffles: unpleasant behaviour with English aboard ship

indicators.note: passengers aboard a vessel are carried inside it, so the pieces sit within

blocks.note: crap is slang for rubbish or nasty conduct
E is the abbreviation for English
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Fights break out when an Englishman behaves badly on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: SS is the conventional abbreviation for steamship; CRAP and E go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapes are minor fights or tussles, the same sense as scuffles or brawls.

clue.text: Oklahoma! Perhaps found by American going via two other states?

indicators.note: a traveller going via a place passes through its middle, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: MI is the postal code for Michigan
US is short for the United States, hence American
CAL is short for California

explanation.surface: A traveller reaches Oklahoma by driving through a couple of neighbouring states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oklahoma!' looks like the state; the exclamation mark marks it as the Rodgers and Hammerstein show. US passes through Michigan, then California follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is a famous stage show with songs, so an example of that theatrical form.

clue.text: Bloke breaking leg in crush

indicators.note: something broken falls into pieces that can be put back in a new order

blocks.note: a bloke is a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man breaks his leg in a crowd surge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crush' looks like a crowd; it is the verb. MAN is followed by LEG broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: To mangle is to damage by crushing or twisting, as rollers squeeze and flatten.

clue.text: Like some cakes put before gourmand finally

indicators.note: what comes finally is at the very end, so just the last letter is kept

blocks.note: to lay something is to put it down
ere is an old word for before
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Some cakes are set down in front of a greedy eater at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put before' reads as serving the cakes to the gourmand, but the two words are separate pieces; ere is an archaic word for before.
explanation.definitionFit: Layered cakes are built from several tiers of sponge with filling between them.

clue.text: Family round fireplace finding fruit

blocks.note: blood relatives are family
O is round in shape
a range is a large cooking stove set in a fireplace

explanation.surface: A family gathered round the hearth comes across some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like 'around', but it gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood orange is a citrus fruit variety with deep red flesh.

clue.text: Judas, in Old English, to hold forth

indicators.note: one thing placed within another sits inside it

blocks.note: a Judas is a traitor, a rat
OE is the abbreviation for Old English

explanation.surface: The story of Judas is to be preached in the old language.
explanation.walkthrough: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, so his name stands for any traitor; the comma hides that 'to hold forth' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak at length in a pompous or formal way, which is what holding forth means.

clue.text: No starter for Ruth whose preference is for fish?

indicators.note: with no start, the opening letter is taken away

blocks.note: ruth is an old word for sorrow or regret

explanation.surface: A dinner guest named Ruth skips the first course because she prefers fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a name, but it is the old noun for pity or regret, the opposite of 'ruthless'; REGRET loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron that wades in shallow water hunting small fish, hence the playful description.

clue.text: Roman historian no end of social climber?

indicators.note: with no end, one extreme letter is removed; here the front one

blocks.note: Livy wrote a vast history of Rome

explanation.surface: A Roman historian is dismissed as an endless social climber.
explanation.walkthrough: LIVY loses an end letter. The question mark flags the definition: a social climber is an upstart, but ivy climbs walls in company.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a clinging evergreen plant that climbs up walls and trees, so a playful kind of climber.

clue.text: Irish with a question: one for Arab

blocks.note: IR is the abbreviation for Irish
taken as written
Q is the abbreviation for question
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An Irishman has a question to put to someone from the Arab world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One for Arab' reads as a question for an Arab; 'one' gives the Roman numeral and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iraqi is a native of Iraq, an Arab country, so an example of an Arab.

clue.text: Power shown by exotic arboreal creature in 1ac

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters are made into an odd new form

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for power
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unusual tree-dwelling animal in the far north displays its strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arboreal creature' reads as one phrase, but 'arboreal' is anagram fodder and 'creature' starts the definition; 1ac refers to the Arctic.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar bear is the large white bear living on the sea ice of the Arctic region.

clue.text: Fire is set in Greene novel

indicators.note: a jewel set in a ring is placed within it, so one piece goes inside another
something novel is new, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A blaze breaks out in a Graham Greene story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greene novel' suggests a book by Graham Greene; 'novel' reworks the name, and IS goes inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to enthuse or invigorate them, and to energise means to fill with vigour.

clue.text: Said condition beginning to deteriorate

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: a state is a condition, as in 'a state of repair'
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A patient's condition is reported to be starting to worsen.
explanation.walkthrough: STATE plus the first letter of the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated means declared or expressed in words, the past tense of speaking formally.
